# Scan rules

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/build-scan-rules.mjs` from server/src/scanner/rules.js. Do not edit by hand; a test fails if it is stale. -->

The scanner **reports; it never blocks**, never calls a tool and never changes a server's data. Every rule is a heuristic over metadata. Ids never change meaning and each has one fixed severity (`info`, `warn`, `high`). Evidence for every finding is the field path, the character span and an excerpt with invisible characters shown as `[U+XXXX]`.

| Id | Severity | Kind | What it catches | Where it looks | What it misses |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MT-CR-001 | high | credential-harvest | Tool description tells the agent to collect passwords, codes or secrets | tool descriptions | Verb plus secret within 60 characters on one line, English only. A schema that simply asks for a password without the description saying so is MT-CR-002 only. |
| MT-CR-002 | warn | credential-harvest | Argument is named like a credential (password, otp, secret, token) | input-schema property names | Names not in the list (a password called "pw" or "k"); it also flags a legitimate login tool. |
| MT-DS-001 | info | oversized-metadata | Unusually long tool description | tool descriptions | Length only (over 2000 characters). It says nothing about content; long text is where a payload can be buried. |
| MT-EX-001 | high | exfil-sink | Argument default points to an off-box URL or address | values under default, const, enum and examples in an input schema | A destination built at call time, a non-URL sink (a file path, a DNS name without a scheme), an off-box URL in the description text rather than a default. Loopback and localhost are treated as on-box. |
| MT-EX-002 | warn | exfil-sink | Argument or skill text asks for sensitive context (credentials, tokens, full conversation) | argument descriptions and A2A skill descriptions | Words outside the list (credentials, tokens, secrets, passwords, API keys, full context). It also fires on honest text such as "do not send a password here"; read the evidence. |
| MT-HI-001 | high | hidden-instruction | Instruction tag in metadata (<IMPORTANT>, <SYSTEM>, ...) | tool descriptions, argument descriptions, resource and prompt text, card text | Other tag names, tags written with look-alike letters, instructions with no tag at all. |
| MT-HI-002 | high | hidden-instruction | Metadata tells the agent to hide something from the user | same as MT-HI-001 | "do not tell/mention/inform/reveal/disclose/notify" only, English only. "Keep this between us" or the same sentence in another language is not matched. |
| MT-HI-003 | high | hidden-instruction | Agent-directed imperative smuggled into metadata | same as MT-HI-001 | A fixed list of phrases ("ignore previous", "before calling any tool", "you must always/first", "always call"). A reworded imperative passes. |
| MT-LM-001 | warn | scan-truncated | Scan truncated: input exceeded a size, depth or count budget | the whole input | It is the scan saying what it did not read: over the depth, value, character or finding budget, or a cycle. The unread part is not judged at all. |
| MT-SA-001 | warn | sensitive-action | Content points the agent at a payment or fund-moving action | resource and prompt text (not tool descriptions) | Fires on any mention of transfer, payment, payout, wire or remit, so a banking prompt trips it; and it misses a money-moving instruction in a tool description. |
| MT-SA-002 | high | sensitive-action | Content tells the agent to bypass approval or consent | resource and prompt text | Bypass wording within 40 characters of approval, consent or authorization; other phrasings and other languages pass. |
| MT-SH-001 | high | name-shadowing | Tool name collides with a trusted tool name | tool names, against the trusted-names list you supply | Nothing without a trusted list: with none, shadowing against other servers cannot be judged. |
| MT-SH-002 | warn | name-shadowing | Tool name is a look-alike of a trusted tool name | tool names, against the trusted-names list | Look-alikes beyond case, separators, accents and a short table of Cyrillic and Greek letters; a one-letter typo is not matched. |
| MT-SH-003 | high | name-shadowing | Description claims primacy over another tool | tool descriptions | Two phrase shapes only ("authoritative ... tool", "ignore any/all other ... tools"). Other ways to claim priority pass. |
| MT-SH-004 | high | name-shadowing | Two tools in one list share a name | one tools/list result | Duplicates across two servers or across two lists (use the trusted list and pinning for that). |
| MT-UC-001 | high | unicode-trick | Bidirectional control characters | every string, including argument names | Only the listed bidirectional marks, embeddings and isolates are matched. It cannot tell legitimate right-to-left text from an attack, so Arabic or Hebrew text that carries explicit marks is flagged. |
| MT-UC-002 | warn | unicode-trick | Zero-width or other invisible characters | every string, including argument names | Invisible characters outside the listed set. A zero-width joiner is reported only between two ASCII characters, so emoji sequences are not flagged. |
| MT-UC-003 | high | unicode-trick | Unicode tag characters (invisible ASCII smuggling) | every string | Only the tag block U+E0000 to U+E007F. Other ways to hide text (a homoglyph, a zero-width encoding) are separate rules. The hidden ASCII is decoded into the detail when it is printable. |
| MT-UC-004 | warn | unicode-trick | Mixed-script word (Latin with Cyrillic or Greek look-alikes) | every string | Words made wholly of look-alike letters (all Cyrillic) are not mixed-script; other scripts are not checked; a legitimate mixed word such as a product name trips it. |

## What a metadata scan does not catch at all

- Result-based injection: a tool whose metadata is clean but whose call RESULT carries the instruction. The scan never calls a tool, so it cannot see results.
- Rug-pulls after the scan: a server can serve a clean list now and a poisoned one later. A scan is a snapshot of one list, one moment. Re-scan, or pin hashes of what you approved.
- Poisoned resources and prompts are only seen if their content was fetched. A metadata-only or offline snapshot scan reads only the names and descriptions it was given.
- The rules are heuristics over known poisoning shapes. A novel phrasing, another language, or an instruction split across fields can slip past, and an unusually worded legitimate tool can trip a flag.
- A clean scan is not proof of safety. It does not judge what a tool does when called, who runs the server, or whether the tool should be allowed at all. Control of the call path is a separate layer.
- A scan of an entitlement-filtered list covers only what that caller sees. A tool hidden from this caller was never scanned, so a clean result is not a clean result for any other caller. (Ping release claim of 2026-11-02, UNVERIFIED on our tenant; the lab only simulates it.)
- The scanner reports. It never blocks a server, changes its data, or stops an agent.
